findings.text: Hyp-mode nonmaskable entry uses a per-CPU nesting record holding a depth count plus a saved hypervisor control value. Outermost entry preserves the control value and ensures trap routing is active, while nested entry only deepens the count. Exit unwinds one level and conditionally restores the preserved control value only when leaving the outermost level. Ordering barriers separate count publication from control save and release, so observers of a nonzero count see a secured configuration and later entrants cannot mistake a stale restore as protection.
Kernel hyp-mode membership is decided by reading the current exception level and testing for level two, with a build-time rejection if compiled for either non-VHE or VHE hypervisor objects.
Spurious interrupt accounting helper accepts an interrupt identifier and increments the global irq_err_count tally.
Huge folio flag cleanup always clears PG_dcache_clean and, when MTE is supported at runtime, also clears PG_mte_tagged plus PG_mte_lock.

The architecture advertises native huge-page table helpers by self-referential capability markers covering creation, access-flag updates, atomic get-and-clear, write protection, flush-on-clear, plain clear, plain get, protection-modify start and commit, hugepage set at range, and migration support.

Huge TLB range flushing maps the incoming stride to a page-table depth: largest folded-aware size uses top-level handling, middle contiguous and normal middle sizes share middle-level handling, small contiguous size uses leaf handling, and any other stride falls back to an unknown-level leaf flush.
Range flushing first widens the caller bounds outward to stride alignment and then delegates to the shared range worker with the normalized interval plus level and flag context.

The shared range worker collapses oversized intervals into a whole-address-space flush and otherwise orders prior stores, derives the address-space identifier, picks an invalidation variant from caching and broadcast options, optionally informs secondary TLB listeners, and optionally synchronizes completion with scope-appropriate barriers.
Requesting TLBF_NOBROADCAST without TLBF_NOWALKCACHE is forbidden and faults, so valid callers combine those options only in supported pairings.

Oversize test uses MAX_TLBI_RANGE_PAGES when range operations exist and otherwise derives a limit from MAX_DVM_OPS scaled by stride, under a stated small worst-case operation assumption for range-capable systems.

Whole-address-space invalidation orders stores, invalidates both the primary and the user address-space identifiers when the kernel is unmapped at EL0, synchronizes stage-one completion including SME handling, and notifies secondary listeners over the full range.
TLBI address values drop the low twelve-bit offset, keep the remaining value to forty-four bits, and place the address-space identifier from bit forty-eight upward.
Stage-one range operation selection forwards caller start, length, stride, identifier and level context to a generic range helper that also accounts for large-address enablement.

Stage-one synchronization orders prior invalidations globally, applies a conditional repeat barrier for a TLBI synchronization erratum, and then performs SME domain synchronization for the target address space.
Repeat synchronization is a no-op unless a specific repeat-TLBI erratum capability is present, in which case it reissues the given invalidation and follows with a global barrier.
SME synchronization has two build forms: one that checks an erratum capability and, when present, synchronizes the CPUs in the address-space mask, and one that is unconditionally empty.
DVMSync delivery returns immediately for an empty CPU mask and otherwise holds preemption disabled across a synchronous cross-call that waits for completion.
Huge-page range flushing derives its stride from the VMA-associated huge-state page size and invokes the huge-range worker with default broadcast and synchronization behavior.

Breakpoint control is a 32-bit bitfield with single-bit enable, two-bit privilege, two-bit type, eight-bit length, and remaining reserved high bits. A breakpoint object pairs 64-bit address plus trigger values with one such control word.

Control translation packs enable lowest, then privilege, then type, then length upward, and sets an additional hypervisor mask bit when running in hyp mode with EL1 privilege. Decoding reverses that packing from low to high bits.
Breakpoint privilege codes distinguish EL1 from EL0 with values one and two, while access-type codes distinguish instruction execution, load, and store with values zero, one, and two.
Breakpoint length masks cover one through eight bytes using progressively wider low-bit populations from a single bit up to eight bits set.
Kernel stepping states are numbered none zero, active one, and suspended two.
Hardware supports sixteen breakpoint and sixteen watchpoint slots. Value and control banks for both kinds are laid out contiguously as four consecutive sixteen-entry groups starting from zero.
Debug register suffixes are bvr, bcr, wvr, and wcr for the four banks, and hyp control adds a mask bit at position thirteen.
Indexed debug register access is offered through read and write helpers that form a system register name from a bank token plus an index and move a 64-bit value to or from a caller variable.

Thread-switch breakpoint handling, hardware-breakpoint inheritance on thread copy, and suspend-time debug restorer installation are all empty operations that accept their arguments and return without effect in these fragments.
Reported breakpoint and watchpoint counts each equal one plus an unsigned field extracted from the sanitized debug feature register using the respective breakpoint or watchpoint shift.

Compatibility capability words use single-bit flags: the first word spans low positions through bit twenty-seven with one combined divide capability formed from two members, and the second word spans low positions through bit six.
Kernel capability indices convert a one-hot hardware mask to a bit number via base-two logarithm, with the second and third banks offset by sixty-four and one hundred twenty-eight.
Native ELF capabilities are read through per-bank CPU getters while compatibility capabilities are read from global compatibility variables, each bank having its own accessor.
Selector CAP_HWCAP is value one, with CAP_COMPAT_HWCAP and CAP_COMPAT_HWCAP2 occupying following values when compatibility is enabled.

Hypervisor symbol handling joins tokens through an indirection, maps names with prefix __kvm_nvhe_ in one build and identity in the other, and emits alias assignments for single symbols and for paired first-second symbols.
Hypervisor sections prefix base names with dot hyp, build a bounding symbol from that full name, and wrap matching inputs between begin and end markers that record the start address.
Protected-guest detection has two builds: one consulting a static branch and one constant false. Hypervisor service initialization is empty, and architecture initialization simply delegates to it.
Boot header is little-endian with a 32-bit code pair first, six 64-bit middle members covering offset size flags plus three reserved slots, and 32-bit magic plus reserve last.

Boot magic is four bytes holding letters A R M plus trailing byte decimal one hundred. Flag layout places endianness at shift zero with single-bit mask, page size at shift one with two-bit mask, and physical-base presence at shift three with single-bit mask. Endianness values are little zero versus big one, page-size values are four-kilobyte one sixteen-kilobyte two sixty-four-kilobyte three, and base presence uses value one.
Flag extraction shifts the flag word right by a field-specific shift and masks to the field width.
Instruction width is four bytes. Monitor breakpoint opcode is 0xd4200000 and fault breakpoint combines that base with FAULT_BRK_IMM shifted left five.

System-hint encodings cover common hints, pointer-authentication helpers, barrier variants, and branch-target-identification forms, each as a small integer shifted left five. Immediate-size, register-role, and register-number categories enumerate data-extraction widths, operand positions, and general-purpose numbers zero through thirty-one with frame-pointer and link-register aliases and a zero-register alias.
Each routed header defines a unique include-once guard macro to prevent multiple inclusion.
Callable TLB maintenance surface includes range flushing with explicit level, huge-range flushing with stride dispatch, huge-page flushing derived from VMA state, and whole-address-space flushing.
